items.text: BLS said producer prices for final demand rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% over 12 months, up from 6.3% in September. Core PPI rose 0.5% (4.9% y/y) and goods prices 0.5% (10.2% y/y), adding to pressure for a Fed hike in December.
items.notes: Closes W-261113-04. Official release read in full; no wire write-up opened.

items.text: The comment period closed on the USCIS proposal to stop officers deferring to earlier approvals when the same employer, worker and facts return in extension petitions (Form I-129, including H-1B). No extension was reported; the current rule stays until a final rule is published.
items.notes: Rule R-261113-03 moves from Open for comment to Proposed. 91 FR 65119; docket USCIS-2026-0529.

items.text: President Nawrocki vetoed the second DSA-implementing law, which would have created a fast procedure for orders blocking illegal online content. He accused the government of blackmail and said a veto was his only option because the Constitutional Tribunal 'does not function'. Digital Affairs Minister Gawkowski said the veto amounts to permission for hate and promised a new online-safety bill.
items.notes: Closes W-261113-05; rule R-261113-01 now Struck down / withdrawn. Framing differs: TVN24 calls it an internet-safety law and leads with Gawkowski; right-wing PCh24 calls it a censorship law and quotes Nawrocki at length. Nawrocki says the Senate widened officials' blocking powers; deputy minister Standerski says there was full court oversight. The companion law naming UKE as digital services coordinator has applied since 6 Nov. The coalition lacks the 3/5 Sejm majority needed to override.

items.text: GUS's flash estimate put Q3 GDP growth at 3.5% y/y (0.8% q/q), down from 4.1% in Q2 and just below the 3.6% consensus. ING called the data dovish for the Monetary Policy Council; PKO BP sees a temporary slowdown.
items.notes: Closes W-261113-07 with the two items below. Detailed breakdown due 30 Nov. ING still expects 50bp of hikes in Q1 2027 but sees risk tilted to none (WNP/PAP).

items.text: GUS confirmed October CPI inflation at 3.5% y/y, unchanged from the flash estimate. ING puts core inflation at 2.9%.
items.notes: Core figure attributed to ING via WNP/PAP; official NBP core release not checked.

items.text: NBP data show a September current-account deficit of 3.1 bn zł, smaller than a year earlier and than forecast. Goods imports reached a record 152.3 bn zł (+14.1% y/y) against exports of 144.4 bn zł (+11.9%).
items.notes: Bankier link seen in search only.

items.text: ePUAP was still switched off on the evening of Nov 13 after the cyberattack, blocking trusted-profile signatures, office inboxes and services such as civil-registry extracts. No restoration date has been given and no attacker country named beyond 'abroad'.
items.notes: Status on Nov 14 not checked.

items.text: The FAA halted departures at every US airport for about four hours on Friday afternoon (roughly 4 to 8:15 p.m. ET) after communications failures at several air route traffic control centres. Transportation Secretary Duffy blamed an outdated, overloaded system and asked Congress for $50 billion to replace it; officials said they did not believe it was a cyberattack.
items.notes: First nationwide ground stop since the 2023 NOTAM failure. Yahoo: 440+ cancellations and 9,000+ delays by 5 p.m. ET (FlightAware). DHS Secretary Mullin called it a telecom outage; the FAA formally had not ruled out a cyberattack. Root cause not yet published.

items.text: Sen. Chris Van Hollen, challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, pledged to end the legislative filibuster and force votes on popular bills. He says at least 10 senators back him; Schumer says he has the votes. The secret-ballot vote is expected in early December.
items.notes: Van Hollen announced Nov 12. Read ABC and Fox; they agree on the facts. Threshold is 28 or 29 votes depending on Alaska. First contested Democratic leadership race since 1994 (Fox).

items.text: Trump threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops a group of about 1,500 mostly Central American migrants walking north from Tapachula. He set no deadline, and Mexico had not responded when Reuters filed.
items.notes: Nov 12, not logged in the previous run. Bessent was reported optimistic on Canada/Mexico deals on Nov 13 (headline only).

items.text: The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President Vance is weighing face-to-face talks with Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei and that Trump has authorised him to negotiate, which cuts against Trump's Nov 12 statement that he took Vance off the talks. Axios reported that Israel's Mossad chief is in Washington pushing for a new campaign against Iran.
items.notes: WSJ and Axios originals not opened. Contested until a second outlet confirms.

items.text: CENTCOM said US forces shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain, with no damage or injuries, and denied the Revolutionary Guards' claim that they had destroyed a US early-warning radar there.
items.notes: 'Confirmed' applies to the CENTCOM statement; the IRGC claim is unverified. Iran called it retaliation for a US strike on a telecom tower in Sirik county.

items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed an LNG carrier hit a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz and that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines. UKMTO says Hormuz traffic is about 65% below pre-war levels.
items.notes: Reuters could not verify the vessels or cause. IEA: Gulf oil shipments 18.4m b/d, 26% below pre-war.

items.text: The administration extended the emergency Jones Act waiver, which lets foreign-flagged ships carry fuel between US ports, for another 90 days ahead of its Nov 15 expiry, according to The National.
items.notes: No official notice seen; link2 is the August extension that set the Nov 15 expiry.

items.text: In a Federalist Society speech, Secretary of State Rubio acknowledged that people are struggling and said the economy should be judged by family affordability, not the stock market, a contrast with Trump's framing, AP noted. He defended the Iran war while conceding it has raised gas prices.
items.notes: AP notes 2028 overtones (possible rivalry with Vance). Analysis by AP.

items.text: Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott asked Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify next month about the Nvidia affair; a White House official said Trump stands by Lutnick amid criticism over chip smuggling to China.
items.notes: Originals not opened.

items.text: Senators Wyden and Alsobrooks opened an investigation into whether HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. misled Congress about his 2019 trip to Samoa before its deadly measles outbreak.
items.notes: AP original not opened.

items.text: A coalition of nonprofits sued Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXAI, asking a court to halt frontier AI development over catastrophic-risk concerns.
items.notes: Politico original not opened. Comes days before Anthropic's Nov 19 first trade.

items.text: PM Tusk said President Nawrocki is keeping up an 'idiotic' situation by not setting a date to swear in Finance Minister Domański as deputy PM and Agnieszka Bartol as funds minister. Tusk said the vacancy hampers talks on the EU's 2028–34 budget before the Nov 26 summit and on finishing the Recovery Plan (KPO).
items.notes: Pełczyńska-Nałęcz resigned Oct 22 but has not been formally dismissed. Palace response not found; only one side read. Nothing new on the NBP board.

items.text: After a Dublin meeting with US envoys Kushner and Witkoff and President Zelensky, European Council President Costa named Europe's team for the US-brokered Ukraine peace talks: EU institutions plus Poland, France, Germany, the UK and Italy. Kushner said Europe would join the next Russia–Ukraine round, expected in Abu Dhabi in about two weeks; Tusk said Poland will play a key role.
items.notes: Also relevant to US–Poland. Euronews quotes Tusk playing down Poland's earlier exclusion from the E3 format and saying Europe will not build a security architecture on what Russia or the US want. A right-wing dlapolski.pl interview frames it more sceptically. No reaction from Nawrocki found.

items.text: Alongside the DSA veto, Nawrocki signed six laws passed on Oct 22: patriotic education, an anti-terrorism amendment, audiovisual production support, the Pharmaceutical Law, VAT and the Central Communication Port (CPK) act.
items.notes: prezydent.pl release could not be fetched. Content of the pharma, VAT and audiovisual changes not checked.

items.text: The signed patriotic-education law requires every pupil to go at least once during their schooling on a trip to memorial or heritage sites, military units or defence firms, and secondary schools to run voluntary engineering clubs. Most provisions apply from 1 Jan 2027.
items.notes: Content from the Sejm-stage article; signature confirmed by LEX.

items.text: The signed anti-terrorism amendment creates a permanent 'special event' status for major state or international events, with mandatory security plans, police processing of participants' data and police or ABW vetting of staff. It takes effect 14 days after publication.
items.notes: Content from the government draft; final text may differ.

items.text: The amendment to the CPK (new central airport) act was signed; a linked ministry draft would extend special planning rules around the airport site.
items.notes: Link between print 3186 and draft UD474 not confirmed.

items.text: A Brussels court overturned Pfizer's seizure of air-navigation fees owed to PANSA, Poland's air-traffic agency, which Pfizer had obtained while enforcing a ruling that Poland must pay over 5.6 bn zł for refused COVID-19 vaccines. The ruling is not final and Pfizer says it is pursuing other enforcement.
Deputy Foreign Minister Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski was charged with misappropriating millions of złoty; he denies the charges.
items.notes: Nov 12, not logged in the previous run. Article seen by the researcher but details not read in full; no Polish-language source checked.

items.text: ZUS warned that its e-services (eZUS, mZUS apps) may be unavailable 09:00–13:00 on Saturday Nov 14 for maintenance.
items.notes: Planned work; no link to the ePUAP attack.

items.text: Poland will miss the Nov 20 deadline to apply the EU's new consumer-credit rules (CCD2); the justice ministry restarted its draft implementing law and has told the Commission it will be late.
items.notes: Source is from Sep 4; no newer status found. Logged as a status check on R-261027-03.

items.text: Holders of 2026 exemptions from Kraków's Clean Transport Zone (SCT) must renew them from Tuesday Nov 17, online (sct.zdmk.krakow.pl or mKraków) or at ZDMK, ul. Centralna 53; checks can take up to 14 days. Under the current resolution, fees from 1 Jan 2027 would be 2.50 zł/hour, 15 zł/day or 250 zł/month unless the planned freeze passes.
items.notes: Covers resident, disabled-card, historic, special and foreign-registered vehicles. Consultation on the fee freeze and tourist fee runs to Nov 27 (krakowskiraport.pl). ZDMK is also studying zone boundary changes.

items.text: Mayor Gibała asked PM Tusk for an urgent 10m zł from the state budget to equip the City Security and Monitoring Centre being built, which will put crisis-management, police, fire and city-guard dispatchers under one roof. Kraków MPs from several parties backed the request.
items.notes: No total cost or opening date given (IKC).

items.text: Horse-drawn carriages return to the Main Square from 11:00 on Saturday, a week after the attack in which carriage drivers and horses were hurt; drivers are asked to take care around the new concrete barriers.
items.notes: Carriage drivers’ association: 4 drivers injured, 2 seriously.

items.text: The Finance Ministry published a draft regulation exempting donations to victims of the Nov 7 attack, and to families of those killed, from inheritance and gift tax for gifts made from 7 Nov 2026 to 31 Dec 2027.
items.notes: Also covers parents of the attacker’s victims in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. RCL page not read.

items.text: Deputy Mayor Karol Wałachowski announced a 'new opening' for Kraków's overdue General Plan: existing drafts are kept, first-stage requests reconsidered, and pre-consultations, physical models and public registers of submissions added. The old land-use study lapsed on Aug 31.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: No new dates. Kraków is at stage 2 of 5. TVP3 headline frames it as starting almost from scratch.

items.text: The Akcja dla Krakowa association petitioned the mayor and council chair to put retractable bollards and number-plate cameras on all Old Town entries, not just the Main and Small Market squares covered by the city's planned 6m zł scheme.
items.notes: City plan (LoveKraków, Nov 9): 25 concrete barriers now, first bollards this year, more in 2027.

items.text: Two free memorial concerts for the victims at St Mary's Basilica on Saturday: Mozart's Requiem by Cappella Cracoviensis at 16:00 and an organ recital by Xaver Varnus at 20:00.

Near ul. Bieżanowska, a 39-year-old man with a previous murder conviction fired at police officers, who fired warning shots; he fled, threw away the pistol and was caught. No one was hurt. Police say he could face a charge of active assault on officers.
items.notes: Not linked to the Main Square attack.

items.text: A private individual asked prosecutors to examine whether police lawfully shot the attacker while he was already on the ground. Voivode Klęczar said he will defend the officers.
items.notes: Prosecutor Piotr Kosmaty wrote on Facebook, as a personal view, that the shots were justified.

items.text: Police detained two men, acting separately, for publicly praising the Nov 7 attack; the voivode said cybercrime units are monitoring online glorification.
A National Prosecutor's Office official told PAP that investigators have established the attacker's route; the motive is still not established.
items.notes: National media give 6 dead and 15–16 injured overall; the voivode’s figure of 11 refers to people still in hospital.

items.text: Stanisław Kułach ('DJ Staszek') registered a Saturday assembly on the Main Square presented as a commemoration; police said they will intervene if the law is broken.
